source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. corrected_answer:
For NCCL variant 28, treat the larger-world-size hang as an observed symptom, not a proven cause. Assume only that the job, exact workload, collective/message shape, and failing world size are reproducible; record NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/launcher/container versions, node/GPU/rank membership and order, TP/PP/EP mapping, InfiniBand versus RoCE mode, NIC and NUMA affinity, selected interface, routing/MTU, topology, rendezvous endpoint, firewall/port policy, timeout settings, and clock synchronization. Keep measured facts separate from estimates and redact sensitive endpoints.

Falsifiable hypothesis: rank mapping and interface/NIC selection exercises a rank pair, fabric path, or communicator step that is absent or safe at smaller world sizes. Hold software, placement policy, workload, message size, and timeout constant; vary one factor at a time (binary-search world size, alternate rank mapping, explicit interface/NIC affinity, or an approved control) and predict that the first failing rank/phase, timeout location, or network counter changes if the factor is causal. A no-change control must remain in the trial set.

Use least-privilege, read-only diagnostics first: collect per-rank NCCL logs with timestamps and communicator phase, launcher/rendezvous membership, topology and NIC mapping, endpoint reachability and authorized firewall/port results, link/error/retransmit counters, and GPU/NIC utilization. Measure communicator-init success, first failing rank/phase, timeout rate, collective latency and bandwidth (ms, GB/s), scaling efficiency (%), retries, correctness, and cleanup duration (s) over repeated matched trials; report n, median and p95/p99 where appropriate, variance/confidence intervals, baseline values, and missing data. Do not claim an improvement from one successful run or from counters without synchronized timestamps.

Rollback: stop the larger-world rollout and restore the last known-good world size, rank/interface mapping, and configuration if any timeout, correctness error, new link error, unhealthy retry loop, or cleanup failure occurs; preserve logs and remove only the canary allocation. Do not change production firewall, routing, drivers, or fabric settings without authorization and a tested rollback. Escalate when evidence does not isolate a causal factor. Required evidence includes raw per-rank logs, exact configuration/software inventory, topology and path artifacts, matched control results, correctness checks, and domain-expert review.

corrected_answer:
For NCCL variant 40, treat the larger-world-size hang as an observed symptom, not a proven cause. Assume only that the job, exact workload, collective/message shape, and failing world size are reproducible; record NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/launcher/container versions, node/GPU/rank membership and order, TP/PP/EP mapping, InfiniBand versus RoCE mode, NIC and NUMA affinity, selected interface, routing/MTU, topology, rendezvous endpoint, firewall/port policy, timeout settings, and clock synchronization. Keep measured facts separate from estimates and redact sensitive endpoints.

Falsifiable hypothesis: reproducible tool-driven triage exercises a rank pair, fabric path, or communicator step that is absent or safe at smaller world sizes. Hold software, placement policy, workload, message size, and timeout constant; vary one factor at a time (binary-search world size, alternate rank mapping, explicit interface/NIC affinity, or an approved control) and predict that the first failing rank/phase, timeout location, or network counter changes if the factor is causal. A no-change control must remain in the trial set.

Use least-privilege, read-only diagnostics first: collect per-rank NCCL logs with timestamps and communicator phase, launcher/rendezvous membership, topology and NIC mapping, endpoint reachability and authorized firewall/port results, link/error/retransmit counters, and GPU/NIC utilization. Measure communicator-init success, first failing rank/phase, timeout rate, collective latency and bandwidth (ms, GB/s), scaling efficiency (%), retries, correctness, and cleanup duration (s) over repeated matched trials; report n, median and p95/p99 where appropriate, variance/confidence intervals, baseline values, and missing data. Do not claim an improvement from one successful run or from counters without synchronized timestamps.

Rollback: stop the larger-world rollout and restore the last known-good world size, rank/interface mapping, and configuration if any timeout, correctness error, new link error, unhealthy retry loop, or cleanup failure occurs; preserve logs and remove only the canary allocation. Do not change production firewall, routing, drivers, or fabric settings without authorization and a tested rollback. Escalate when evidence does not isolate a causal factor. Required evidence includes raw per-rank logs, exact configuration/software inventory, topology and path artifacts, matched control results, correctness checks, and domain-expert review.
